_doc: ⚑ S392 (UiB job 26 Part B0–B2; S390 before it) — THE THREE TVs: where each glass is, how big its canvas is, which era owns it, where the piece's margin panel hangs, and the conducted moment's pacing. The bodies are room props (data/room/reinterp_deltas.json: tvDresser… in r1, wallTv… in r3, e26Display… in r4) so they age and glob with their rooms; only the glass is src/room/teachingTv.ts's own screen (makeScreenTexture 'screen', the S80 exception). `facing` is the glass normal: south = +z, north = −z, east = +x, west = −x. `pos` is the glass centre in world metres, 3 mm proud of its tube prop. `seat` is the seat's eye (the probes' seat poses). Measured from the seat (tools/s392-tv-probe.mjs): 1997 122° right of the desk at 2.0 m (behind and to one side, clear of the flip's 180°), 2016 90° left of the desk at 1.66 m (the south wall, square on), 2026 59° left of the desk at 1.6 m (on a wall arm beside the shelf, forward of the old monitor's face).

1997._docPicture: a 4:3 tape on a 4:3 set: the picture fills the glass; the VCR's own on-screen display draws over it only while it is paused or stopped

2016._docPicture: a 16:9 disc on a 16:9 wall TV: the DVD player's own on-screen display when paused (his "this was a DVD": no skip button anywhere; during the disc's trailers the only control is pause)

2026._docPanel: ⚑ S392 — the margin panel hangs 0.72 m from the eye here, not 1.2 m, and is 0.6× the size (its letters keep their 1.45°): at 1.2 m the old monitor on the plank and her headset on its stand stood between the seat and the panel (the probe's photos).
2026._docPicture: a 16:9 film on a 2026 display in a retro body: the share line Dad's link arrives under, and the display's own overlay controls when paused

panel._doc: ⚑ S392 (UiB job 26 B2) — THE MARGIN AND THE CAPTIONS, DRAWN LIVE, in the record's style (RECORD palette, the Fixedsys Excelsior face), as the piece's voice and clearly not the tape's. Job 25 measured the tapes' burned-in text from the seat at 0.4–0.8° in the headset and 3–6 px on a phone; text that reads needs a capital height of at least 1.0° in the headset, 12 px on a phone and 14 px on the computer. A 42° vertical field of view makes the phone (390 CSS px tall, landscape) the hardest: 12 px is 1.29° on paper, and the probe measured 1.32° at 11.4 px on the emulated phone, so every capital is drawn at `capDeg` = 1.45° from the seat (12.5 px on the phone). The panel is 0.9 m wide (34 characters a line at that size) and holds nine lines; a cue whose own line breaks would take more than seven is flowed as one paragraph (the probe found 2026's first label frame at 11 lines). At the TVs' own distances (1.7–2.1 m) that is 4–5 cm per capital, which no glass can carry with a picture above it (B2's first option measured worse), so the text hangs on its own panel in front of the TV, `dist` metres from the seat's eye, just under the TV in the view (`gapDeg` below the glass's lower edge), facing the seat. The panel's background is drawn only behind the lines that are up, so it is sized to what it says. It is shown only while the tape is in play or paused and a caption or a margin line belongs to that second, and its canvas uploads only when its words change.

moment._doc: The conducted moment's clock. A turn runs at the room turn's own pace (e4Room: 52° in 9.2 s, smoothstep, peak 8.5°/s, inside the comfort law's 9.1°/s), clamped; ⚑ S392: `turnMax` 16 → 22, because 1997's TV is now 122° behind the seat and 16 s would have peaked at 11.4°/s (a smoothstep peaks at 1.5× its average): 122° × 0.177 = 21.6 s peaks at 8.5°/s; in a headset every conducted move is one cut under the dissolve (app.ts startCamMove). `arriveHold` = the TV is on, its leader on the glass, before the turn (2026: Dad's link); `callHold` = the longest Lamby's call (1997, 2016) is given to be read before the piece turns the visitor anyway (its Take me there turns at once); `afterHold` = the end card held, paused, before the return to the desk. `afterDad` = the seconds Dad's two lines are given before his link (readHold of the pair is 3.9 s).
